digest.component_or_area: RP-04 secrets and authentication architecture research
propositions: Rebar must safely support credential injection for Bedrock, OpenAI, Anthropic, Gerrit, GitHub, GitLab, Jenkins, and Jira variants across local, CI, AWS-hosted, CLI, library, MCP, and hosted-service environments without a universal secret broker or weakened SDK-native refresh and rotation.

Current bridge-runner unfiltered environment propagation exposes unrelated provider credentials to reconciler, delivery, and sibling subprocesses; subprocess handling must remove exact Rebar-declared secret names for siblings and overlay static values only to owning children.

Static credential rotation for long-running processes requires restart or redeploy; deployment supplies pre-resolved secrets at startup (file or environment) rather than Rebar performing runtime SSM retrieval, refresh, or hot-reload.

Operation snapshots must remain structurally unable to contain credentials; provider-native pre-client capabilities (AccessTokenProvider, workload identity, session objects) are injected into Rebar-owned factories; Pydantic SecretStr/SecretBytes wrap only unavoidable static adapter-local carriers with repr/comparison/hash exclusion.
Authenticated operations fail closed without fallback to ambient or anonymous identity; missing or revoked credentials block the operation rather than weakening the security posture.
